title: Decoupage, paint finishes and repeat patterns that last

say: Decoupage, paint finishes, and repeat patterns that last.
This is the video for module two of Advanced Home Décor and Upcycling.
A plain tray, jar, stool or cushion can be transformed by its surface. Advanced decoupage has edges that disappear, no bubbles, and a surface smooth enough to wipe.

say: Sand wood with 120, then 180 grit, and wipe off the dust. A white or light base coat makes prints show true colour.

panel.heading: Prepare, apply, then bury the edge
items: Sand wood 120 then 180; light base coat
Use the thin printed layer of a napkin
Glue on the surface, smooth from centre
Thin coats, light wet sand after about four

say: Thin paper makes edges vanish. Peel the plain back layers off a printed napkin and keep only the top. Torn edges blend better than cut ones.

panel.heading: Prepare, apply, then bury the edge
items: Sand wood 120 then 180; light base coat

say: Brush a thin coat of medium, or PVA glue diluted about 3 parts glue to 1 part water, onto the surface, not the paper. Smooth from the centre outwards, through cling film, to push out air.

say: Then thin coats, each in a different direction. After about four, sand very gently with wet 400 grit paper, only flattening ridges, and keep coating.

say: Every faux finish layers a base colour and a contrasting top colour. For dry brushing, wipe almost all paint off the brush, then sweep lightly. Paint catches only the raised parts.

panel.heading: Five paint effects to master
items: Dry brushing: highlights raised parts
Colour wash: 1 part paint to 3 or 4 water
Sponging: a stone look
Distressing: sand edges to show dark base
Crackle: top coat over tacky medium

say: A colour wash thins paint with water so the wood grain shows. Sponging dabs a second colour, rotating the sponge to avoid a repeating mark.

panel.heading: Five paint effects to master
items: Dry brushing: highlights raised parts
Colour wash: 1 part paint to 3 or 4 water
Sponging: a stone look
Distressing: sand edges to show dark base
Crackle: top coat over tacky medium

say: Distressing sands the edges and corners to reveal a dark base. For crackle, brush the top colour over crackle medium, or PVA glue, while it is still tacky. Never mix water-based and oil-based paint.

say: Ready-made chalk paint is costly. A home recipe uses 1 part plaster of Paris, 1 part cool water, and 3 parts emulsion paint, by volume.

panel.heading: Grace mixes chalk-style paint
items: Recipe: 1 plaster, 1 water, 3 emulsion
Plans 800 ml: 800 / 5 = 160 ml per part
160 ml plaster + 160 ml water, smooth
Mix into 480 ml emulsion; stir between coats

say: For example, Grace in Jos needs about 750 ml for two stools. To be safe she plans for 800 ml. That is 5 parts, so 160 ml per part.

say: She stirs 160 ml of plaster into 160 ml of water until smooth, then mixes it into 480 ml of emulsion. It thickens, so she stirs before coat 2.

say: PVA glue and most varnishes are not tested as safe for food. Decorate only the back of clear glass plates or the outside of jars, and label items: wipe clean, do not soak, decorative use.

cards.d: Decoupage is not food-safe and softens if soaked. Never sell decoupage plates, bowls or cups for eating.
Mix and sand outdoors or by an open window, wear a dust mask, keep children away. Never pour plaster down a sink.
Cut away from your body and other hand, use a metal ruler, cap the knife, wrap used blades in tape.

say: Plaster and sanded paint make fine dust. Work outdoors or by an open window, wear a dust mask, and keep children away. Never pour leftover plaster down a sink.

say: A pattern looks professional when it fits evenly, with no half-motif squeezed in at one edge. For example, Chioma in Enugu prints cushion covers 45 cm square. With a 1 cm border on each side, she has 43 cm to print.

panel.heading: Chioma's four cushion covers
items: 45 cm cover, 1 cm border: 43 cm to print
5 motifs of 7 cm = 35 cm
8 cm left for 4 gaps: 2 cm each
Wash and iron first; chalk the grid
Dry 24 hours, then heat-set with an iron

say: Her block is 7 cm. Five motifs take 35 cm, leaving 8 cm for 4 gaps: 2 cm each. If it does not divide evenly, adjust the gaps, not the motif.

say: She washes and irons the covers first, marks a chalk grid, and after 24 hours drying, heat-sets them as the paint label directs.

say: For stencils, dab most of the paint off onto paper towel first, and build colour in light layers. And remember, a block prints in mirror image, so carve letters reversed.

panel.rule: Off-load the brush. Too much paint makes it bleed.

say: To remember. Thin paper and many thin coats bury the edges. Faux finishes layer two colours. Mix chalk paint one, one, three. Fit repeats by adjusting the gaps. Test every finish on a sample first.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Thin paper, torn edges, many thin coats
Base plus contrasting top colour
Chalk paint: 1 plaster, 1 water, 3 emulsion
Adjust gaps so repeats fit
Decoupage is decorative, not food-safe
